samples.summary: Toolbar style dropdown makes the retained heading level invisible and destroys it via an already-checked menu item
samples.evidence: `getBlockType()` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2786-2797) now returns `{type:'list-item', headingLevel:2}` for a bulleted heading. `text-style-group.tsx:86` -> `getBlockLabel` (text-style-options.ts:112) and `:89` -> `blockTypeToStyleId` (text-style-options.ts:127) both gate on `type === 'heading'`, so the trigger reads "Normal text" and `currentStyleId` is `normal`. The dropdown therefore renders "Normal text" as already **checked** (`text-style-group.tsx:128`) — yet clicking that seemingly no-op item calls `setBlockType('paragraph')`, which is the one command that permanently clears the remembered `headingLevel` (memory.ts:250-256 / yorkie-doc-store.ts:1452-1456). The user has no UI affordance showing the level is retained, and the least-suspicious click in the menu silently discards it. Fix belongs in the toolbar consumer (label/checked state) or by making the paragraph command preserve the level.

samples.summary: Table-cell Backspace bypasses Doc.deleteBackward, so the new heading-restoring list exit does not hold inside table cells (while Enter does)
samples.evidence: `handleBackspace` intercepts cell-internal blocks at packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:1895-1926 and never calls `this.doc.deleteBackward(...)` — it merges with the previous block in the cell or no-ops. The diff's new exit lives in `Doc.deleteBackward` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:262-270), so an empty bulleted Heading 2 in a table cell does NOT come back as a heading on Backspace. Enter in the same cell *does* route through `docSplitBlock` -> `Doc.splitBlock` (text-editor.ts:2049) and therefore restores the heading, so the two keys now disagree inside cells — exactly the Enter/Backspace parity the change set out to establish.

samples.summary: Unchanged line in YorkieDocStore.setBlockType still assumes headingLevel exists only on headings when computing the post-change style id
samples.evidence: `const nextHeadingLevel = type === 'heading' ? (opts?.headingLevel ?? 1) : undefined; const nextBlock = { ...block, type, headingLevel: nextHeadingLevel }` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1400-1401) builds a block that no longer matches what the same method actually writes to the tree/cache a few lines later (`keepHeadingLevel` retains the level, :1413/:1458). It is benign today only because `blockStyleId` maps `list-item` -> `normal` (packages/docs/src/model/named-styles.ts:99-113); the moment any style logic consults a retained level, this store diverges from `MemDocStore.setBlockType`, which computes `blockStyleId(block)` *after* mutation with the level present (packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:272). Cheap fix: derive `nextBlock` from the same `keepHeadingLevel` decision.

samples.summary: No export path carries the retained heading level, so a bulleted heading loses it on any DOCX/PDF/Markdown round trip
samples.evidence: Every exporter gates strictly on `type === 'heading'`: docx-exporter.ts:184 (`block.type === 'heading' ? block.headingLevel : undefined`), pdf-exporter.ts:202 (outline filter `b.type === 'heading'`), serialize/markdown.ts:103-106. DOCX *import* can never produce a `list-item` at all (docx-style-map.ts:132-148 only emits `heading`/`paragraph`; docx-importer.ts:242). So export→import of a document containing a bulleted heading returns a plain bullet, and un-bulleting it after the round trip yields a paragraph — the model state the change adds is silently non-portable. Acceptable if intended (the todo lists DOCX pStyle as a non-goal), but no exporter or importer consumer was updated or documented as lossy.

samples.summary: applySplitBlock is a public package export whose contract now leaks headingLevel to any external caller splitting into a list-item
samples.evidence: `applySplitBlock` is re-exported from packages/docs/src/index.ts:84 and packages/docs/src/node.ts:110, and `DocStore.splitBlock(id, offset, newId, newBlockType)` is public API (packages/docs/src/store/store.ts). With the new `newBlockType !== 'list-item'` clause, any caller that splits a *heading* block while requesting a `list-item` result now gets a list-item carrying the source heading's level, which will later re-materialize as a heading on un-bullet. In-repo callers are safe (`Doc.splitBlock` only picks `'list-item'` when the source is already one — packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:328-337), so this only affects external/embedding consumers of the package.
